title: The Forgotten Server
question: Has svc-billing been used interactively outside the application systems it is meant to support?
briefing: There is no incident alert. Start a planned account review, compare its usual host with observed relationships, and choose where to narrow your hunt. Establish the billing dependency before recommending any disruption.

facts.title: Expected account purpose
facts.text: svc-billing runs the scheduled billing batch from APP-01. This review asks where the account has been used; no security alert initiated it.

facts.title: Expected relationship
facts.text: svc-billing has scheduled batch authentication on APP-01 in the review window.

facts.title: A connection outside the usual path
facts.text: svc-billing also has an interactive session, BILL-S1, on LEGACY-01 at step 0. The host is absent from current inventory. Neither detail establishes misuse.

facts.title: An undocumented business dependency
facts.text: Billing Operations confirms LEGACY-01 supplies the nightly billing batch. No managed-host isolation capability is available. Do not stop it on the strength of its age or inventory absence. Session restrictions belong to the response team.

facts.title: A matching migration record
facts.text: Approved migration CR-204 covers svc-billing, LEGACY-01, operator OP-14, this maintenance interval and the interactive billing-validation task. An approval alone does not prove who used the account.

facts.title: No matching approval in the covered register
facts.text: The covered change register contains no task authorising svc-billing interactive use on LEGACY-01 in this interval. This is one source, not proof of compromise by itself.

facts.title: Approval archive unavailable
facts.text: The older change archive is unavailable for this interval. No matching approval can be verified or ruled out.

facts.title: Session origin corroborates the task
facts.text: The separate management-gateway record maps BILL-S1 to OP-14 on MGMT-01 and the CR-204 billing-validation operation. It corroborates the specific approval, not every possible later action.

facts.title: A distinct origin outside the permitted route
facts.text: The management gateway attributes BILL-S1 to an unmanaged client outside the registered migration route. Operator identity is unverified. Combine this with task or application evidence before claiming misuse.

facts.title: Authentication does not establish an operator
facts.text: The legacy gateway retained authentication only. There is no usable operator or process-origin mapping for BILL-S1.

facts.title: Recorded migration task origin
facts.text: At step 2, host task collection records the approved billing-validation task created from BILL-S1 with the matching CR-204 operation identifier.

facts.title: Recorded persistent task outside approved work
facts.text: At step 2, host task collection records BILL-S1 creating a recurring export task with no registered migration identifier. This is a distinct host observation, not another copy of the authentication entry.

facts.title: Historical process collection was absent
facts.text: LEGACY-01 has no historical process-creation collection at this cutoff. Enabling it now can record future executions only; it cannot recover an earlier task origin.

facts.title: Billing application records expected access
facts.text: At step 6 the billing application records the scoped reconciliation dataset requested by the approved validation task. It does not establish activity outside this application.

facts.title: A second source records consequential access
facts.text: At step 6 the billing application records BILL-S1 requesting a customer-export dataset outside the migration task scope. The application records access scope independently of host-task collection.

facts.title: Application detail was not collected
facts.text: Application collection cannot attribute the reviewed data action to BILL-S1. Missing activity detail does not establish that no access occurred.

queries.label: Compare account activity by host
queries.can: Reveal recorded account-to-host relationships in the review window.
queries.cannot: Inventory absence and interactive use do not establish intent.

queries.label: Inspect session origin
queries.can: Check an independently recorded operator and task route.
queries.cannot: An unfamiliar client alone does not prove misuse.

queries.label: Check ownership and billing dependency
queries.can: Establish the business dependency and permitted response capability.
queries.cannot: An undocumented host is not automatically safe to shut down.

queries.label: Check the migration approval
queries.can: Compare account, host, operator, time and task.
queries.cannot: An approval does not authorise every later action.

queries.label: Inspect task provenance
queries.can: Inspect recorded process creation through the requested cutoff.
queries.cannot: A new sensor cannot backfill historical task origin.

queries.label: Inspect billing application scope
queries.can: Read application access scope from its own collection path.
queries.cannot: This source cannot identify all activity on the host.

queries.label: Review the future observation window
queries.can: Read executions recorded while the explicitly enabled sensor was active.
queries.cannot: A future execution is not a recovered creation event.

events.description: A task is created from the reviewed session.
The scheduled task requests application access.
A scheduled task executes; any available sensor records this execution only.
The APP-01 billing batch completes through the legacy dependency.
The data objective requires the prepared access and still-active reviewed session.

truth.B: The specific migration was approved. The legacy billing dependency was real.
truth.M: The reviewed session created an unauthorised persistent task. The billing dependency was still real.
truth.U-B: The unobserved legacy activity was benign migration support. The available records did not establish that.
truth.U-M: The unobserved legacy activity was unauthorised. Its matched visible records did not establish that.
